identity.title: You & your background
identity.text: These details are used everywhere in Made2Found – your founder profile, co-founder search and Connect. You only need to keep them up to date here.
identity.name: Name
identity.headline: Headline
identity.headlineHint: One sentence about what you do.
identity.bioHint: What should people know about your work?
identity.regionHint: A rough area is enough: Berlin, Rhine-Main, North Rhine-Westphalia.
identity.publishedNote: Your Connect profile is published. Changes here are visible there immediately.
identity.rolesHint: This controls which areas are offered to you – not what you have access to. What you can see as an advisor stays tied to the teams that invited you.

roles.founder: Founder – I'm founding or looking for co-founders

identity.publishTitle: Still needed before you can publish:
identity.publishNote: You can save at any time – this only applies if you want your profile visible to others in Connect or in co-founder search.

gaps.displayName: A name with at least {min} characters
gaps.headline: A headline with at least {min} characters
gaps.bio: A short introduction with at least {min} characters

identity.photoVisibleLabel: Make my photo visible to signed-in members
identity.photoVisibleHint: Your Made2Found profile photo then appears wherever members see you – in co-founder search, in connections and in teams. If unchecked, only you see it. This doesn't apply to Connect: there you decide separately whether your photo appears, and Connect gets its own copy.

linkedin.title: LinkedIn
linkedin.urlHint: Your profile's web address. You can copy it straight from the address bar – we'll add the “https://”. LinkedIn addresses only.
linkedin.urlInvalid: We don't recognize that as a LinkedIn profile. It needs to be an address at linkedin.com, for example linkedin.com/in/your-name.
linkedin.visibilityTitle: Who should see your LinkedIn profile?

private.label: Nobody but you
private.hint: The address is saved but shown nowhere. Useful if you want it on file and decide later.

contacts.label: People you are connected to
contacts.hint: Only people who have accepted a contact request with you – people you're already in touch with.

members.label: Everyone signed in to Made2Found
members.hint: Anyone with an account here who is signed in. Not the open web, but not just your inner circle either.

public.label: Outside Made2Found too
public.hint: On your public network page, which anyone can open without an account.

linkedin.publicWarning: Anyone on the internet can open that page, and search engines index it. People could then find your LinkedIn profile by searching for your name.
linkedin.publicConfirm: Yes, my LinkedIn profile may appear on my public page.
linkedin.openHint: Opens LinkedIn in a new window

cv.title: Import from your CV (optional)
cv.betaNote: Still in beta: for now this only works with copy and paste – welcome back to the 2000s 😉 Reading files directly is coming soon.
cv.text: Paste your CV as text. The tool marks which skills and industries it recognizes – you decide what goes into your profile.
cv.privacyNote: Your CV stays in your browser. It is not uploaded, not sent to an AI, and not stored anywhere. Once you leave the page it's gone.
cv.placeholder: Paste it here – Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C in your PDF, then Ctrl+V here.
cv.tooShort: That's not enough text to find anything useful yet. Go ahead and paste your whole CV.
cv.nothingFoundHint: That says nothing about your background – the tool only knows a fixed list of words. Just add your skills and industries above yourself.
cv.applied: Added – check the fields above, then save.
cv.fileUnsupported: We can't read that file. Only plain text works (.txt or .md) – for a PDF or Word document, it's best to copy the contents straight into the field.

photo.title: Your photo
photo.help: A picture or an illustration. You decide below who can see it – and separately in Connect.

evidence.title: What's the last task you were responsible for and saw through to the end?
evidence.text: A concrete example says more about your experience than a list of keywords. It doesn't have to come from a job – your own project, volunteering or a side job count just as much.
evidence.narrativeLabel: What was it about, and which part was yours?
evidence.narrativePlaceholder: For example: I took our first enterprise customer from first contact to a signed contract – the proposal, follow-up questions and negotiation were my responsibility.
evidence.narrativeHint: Two or three sentences are enough. At least {min} characters.
evidence.levelLabel: And how much experience do you have in that area overall?
evidence.assignmentNote: I'll suggest an area for it in the next step – you decide whether to confirm it.

confirm.title: Here's what I took from it
confirm.text: I only go by the words in your text – that can be right, or just as easily wrong. So I'd rather ask: which of these was really your strength?
confirm.noneIsFine: If none of these fit, just don't select any. You can choose the area yourself in the next step.
confirm.emptyText: I couldn't match your text to an area. That says nothing about your description – my list of terms is limited and misses paraphrases. You'll choose the area yourself in the next step.

engine.rules: Matched using a fixed list of terms in your browser, without an AI model. Your text isn't sent anywhere for this.
engine.model: Matched by an AI model. The result may be wrong – your selection is what counts.

areas.title: Which other areas have you worked in?
areas.text: Start with the fields you've actually worked in. The specific areas appear after that. Focus on what matters, not everything you've ever touched.

ownership.title: Which of these do you not want to own long term?
ownership.text: Being able to do something doesn't mean wanting to be responsible for it long term. It's worth discussing that difference early.
ownership.noEntries: You have not selected any areas yet.

levels.label: Experience
levels.5: Applied even in difficult situations; can support others

ownershipWishes.label: Responsibility
ownershipWishes.grow_into: I want to grow into it
ownershipWishes.prefer_external: I'd rather have it covered externally

summary.title: What you bring
summary.empty: Your overview appears here once you've completed the snapshot.
summary.incompleteNote: Anything not listed here just means you have not entered it yet.
summary.removeEvidenceQuestion: Remove this evidence? The text will be deleted for good.

readout.title: What this shows
readout.coverage: {areas} areas recorded, {levelled} of them with an experience level and {wished} with a responsibility preference.
readout.focus: Most of your entries are in {family}.
readout.basis: This summary only puts your own entries side by side – experience level and responsibility preference. It doesn't interpret them, and an empty field only means nothing has been entered there.

anchor.title: Responsibility you want to take on
anchor.text: In these areas, you want to be in charge for the long term. When you talk about founding together, this is the starting point for dividing up roles.

canButHandsOver.title: You have experience – but would rather hand over responsibility
canButHandsOver.text: In these areas, you have hands-on experience but don't want to be responsible for them long term. That isn't a contradiction – it's important input for dividing up roles: you can support here, but responsibility should sit with someone else.

growingInto.title: Responsibility you want to grow into
growingInto.text: You want to take on responsibility here but don't have much experience yet. That can be planned for – if it's discussed openly.

contributes.title: Contributing without being in charge
contributes.text: You're involved here but don't want to be in charge. That tends to make dividing up roles easier, not harder.

undecided.title: Still open
undecided.text: You haven't stated a responsibility preference here, or you've explicitly left it open. A good place to start a conversation.

comparison.title: If you were to start a company together
comparison.intro: This isn't an assessment or a compatibility score. It puts your entries side by side and sorts them by what should be settled before starting a company.
comparison.basis: It's based on two self-reports – experience level and responsibility preference. It's a starting point for conversation, not a test, and it doesn't predict success.
comparison.coverage: {together} areas in total, {shared} of them entered by both of you, {onlyA} only by you, {onlyB} only by {name}.
comparison.gapNote: Where entries are missing, nothing is shown. That can mean not entered – or not shared. We deliberately don't distinguish between the two; otherwise holding back would itself say something.

overlap.high: You've both entered something almost everywhere – a lot of overlap in what you bring. It's worth looking together at whether there are areas neither of you covers.
overlap.balanced: Your entries partly overlap and partly complement each other.
overlap.low: You've entered hardly any of the same areas – you complement each other strongly. It's worth talking about what each of you actually does in your own areas.

contested.title: Both of you want to own it
contested.text: You both claim the same responsibility here. Who takes it on isn't settled yet – this is something to discuss with each other.

openPosition.title: Nobody wants to own it
openPosition.text: Neither of you wants to be in charge of this long term. Whether that's a problem depends on what your venture needs – and we don't know that. All we can say is that nobody is in charge here yet.

bothShallow.title: Wanted, but no deep experience yet
bothShallow.text: At least one of you wants to take this on, and neither of you has stated deep experience here. As a team, you have little experience in this area.

handoverPath.title: A path that can be planned
handoverPath.text: One of you has deep experience here and doesn't want to keep it; the other wants to take it on but isn't there yet. That can be planned for – once it's said out loud.

settled.title: Already settled
settled.text: One of you wants the responsibility and has the experience for it; the other doesn't want it. Nothing to negotiate here – just to name.

noBasis.title: Not enough to go on
noBasis.text: There isn't enough information on these areas to say anything. That's a statement about the data, not about you.

comparison.empty: There isn't enough information yet for a comparison with {name}. That may be because of either of your snapshots, or because of how much of them is shared.
comparison.sectionText: You can put your snapshot side by side with those of people you're connected to – ordered by what should be settled before starting a company.
comparison.noneYet: Once a contact request has been accepted, the person appears here.

areaLabels.owning_outcomes: Seeing something through to a result
areaLabels.structuring_work: Organizing work so others can plug in

errors.narrative: Please write at least two short sentences.
errors.save: That couldn't be saved just now. Please try again.
errors.published_incomplete: Your published Connect profile needs a name, a headline and a slightly longer text about you. Please fill in what's missing, or switch your Connect profile back to draft first.
errors.roles: At least one role has to stay selected. Without a role, there's no area the platform can take you to.
errors.linkedin: We can't recognize that as a LinkedIn profile. It has to point to linkedin.com – so we haven't saved it.
errors.strength_length: One sentence, at most two hundred characters.
errors.resource_empty: Please choose a type and add a short sentence.
errors.photo_empty: Please choose a picture or an illustration.
errors.photo_too_large: That picture is too large. Please choose a smaller one.
errors.photo_save: The photo could not be saved.

success.interview_done: The conversation is finished. Your answers are ready to be sorted into areas.

contexts.title: Where you decide what is shown
contexts.text: Your details are stored here. Whether and how they appear in each area, you decide there.

disclosure.title: Who gets to see what you can do?
disclosure.text: Above, you noted what you have experience in. Here you decide who gets to see any of it. Unless you change this, nobody does.
disclosure.privateHint: Your entries stay with you. Others can't even tell that you've filled anything in.
disclosure.areasHint: Your profiles will then show what you have experience in – in your case {examples}, for instance. Nothing more: how much experience you have, and what you'd like to take on, stays with you.
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contact: People you're connected with see more
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contactHint: Everyone else still sees only the topics. Anyone whose connection request you've accepted also sees how much experience you have – and what you'd like to take on and what you'd rather not.
disclosure.note: Two things always apply: nobody ever sees your evidence. And public pages – the ones anyone on the web can open – never show any of this.
disclosure.privateNotFound: As long as your areas are private, you won't show up in searches by skill. That's not a drawback, it's your choice — people can still find you through everything else in your profile.

notices.recognised: We've matched your description to one or more areas – already checked below. See if that fits, and add anything that's missing.
notices.unmatched: We couldn't match your description to an area yet. It's saved under “Other focus” – choose the area below that actually fits.
notices.confirmed: Your selection is saved. You can add anything that's still missing here.
notices.interview_paused: Saved. You can pick up the conversation where you left off at any time.

interview.title: The conversation
interview.text: Eight questions about situations that actually happened – at work and outside it. No test, no points: your stories become suggestions for which areas you cover, and you confirm each one yourself.
interview.guidanceTime: Plan on 30 to 45 minutes if you do it in one go. But it's deliberately not meant to be clicked through quickly – two questions in one evening is perfectly fine.
interview.guidanceSaving: Everything is saved automatically while you write. If your browser crashes or you close the window, your text will be there next time. You can also save at any point and continue later.
interview.guidanceDictate: You can type or dictate – the microphone on your keyboard is enough, you do not need to switch anything on.
interview.guidanceLength: Two to five sentences are enough. Tell it the way you would tell somebody at the kitchen table, with names, numbers and the parts that went wrong.
interview.guidanceNoRight: There are no right answers. “I don't know” is an answer too – in that case, just skip the question.
interview.privacy: Nobody but you sees what you share here. Later, a team summary includes only which area you confirmed and where you stand on it – never the story behind it.
interview.contextEither: At work or in your personal life – both count equally here
interview.resumeEmpty: Your conversation is open, but there's no question in it yet. One click loads it.
interview.answerPlaceholder: Tell it the way you would tell somebody at the kitchen table – with names, numbers and the parts that went wrong.
interview.saveStateFailed: Couldn't save just now – your text is kept in this browser. Leave the window open; we'll keep trying.
interview.restored: A version in this browser was longer than the saved one – we've restored it. Please check that it's right.
interview.followUpHint: If you like, you can go into this too – just add it to your answer above.
interview.tooShort: At least {min} characters – otherwise there's nothing to work with. If nothing comes to mind, skip the question.
interview.completeTextAll: You've gone through all the questions. Finishing closes the conversation; your answers are kept and will be sorted into areas in the next step.
interview.completeTextEnough: You've answered enough ({min} or more) for a summary. You can also keep going – the more situations, the more precise it gets.

errors.start: The conversation could not be opened. Please try again.
errors.save: The answer could not be saved. Your text is still in the field.
errors.stale: This question is out of date – maybe a second window was open. Here's where things stand now.
errors.complete: Couldn't finish the conversation. Please try again.

interview.sortPending: {count, plural, one {One answer is waiting to be sorted} other {# answers are waiting to be sorted}}

sort.title: Sort your answers
sort.remaining: {count, plural, one {One answer is not sorted yet} other {# answers are not sorted yet}}
sort.whichAreasText: Up to three. If none of the suggestions fits, don't pick any – your story is kept either way and goes under “Other”.
sort.fromQuestionHint: This is not a finding in your text: if you have any story at all for this question, you've done it. You still need to confirm it.
sort.nothingFound: Nothing was recognized here. That says nothing about your story – only that it didn't match our list of terms. You can add areas yourself later in your profile.
sort.limit: Up to {max} areas. If you check everything, it no longer says anything.
sort.emptyAllowed: It's fine to continue without a selection.
sort.doneText: No answer is left open. What you confirmed is now in your profile – with your story attached as evidence.
sort.alreadySorted: This answer was already sorted – perhaps a second window was open. Here is the next one.
sort.againTitle: {count, plural, one {One answer is already sorted} other {# answers are already sorted}}
sort.againText: You can sort an answer again. That's useful if the suggestions were thin at the time – recognition keeps improving, while your story stays the same. The old evidence is replaced so the same story doesn't appear twice in your profile. Areas you've already confirmed stay.
sort.fromModelHint: Every suggestion comes with the exact sentence it's based on – checked against your answer when it was saved. Anything a model can't back up never shows up here. Whether it's right is your call.
sort.levelFor: How much experience do you have in “{area}”?
sort.askTitle: Let the AI take a look?
sort.askText: A language model on our own hardware reads only this answer and suggests areas – each with the sentence it's based on. It doesn't decide anything, doesn't set a level, and sees no other answer. You can also do the sorting entirely without it.
sort.ask: Let the AI read this answer
sort.askRunning: The AI is reading. That usually takes less than twenty seconds – this page refreshes on its own.
sort.askUnavailable: No model is available right now. That's not an error: it runs on a machine that's sometimes switched off. Just sort without it – or come back later.
sort.ownChoiceHint: All areas, grouped by field. Pick what's true – even if none of it was suggested above. Our recognition depends on words; your story doesn't.

errors.area: One of the areas is unknown. Please reload the page and try again.
errors.save: Sorting couldn't be saved. Your answer hasn't changed.
errors.link: Saved, but the answer could not be marked as sorted. It will appear once more – please do not sort it twice.
errors.resort: Couldn't open it. Your answer and its sorting haven't changed.
errors.ask: The request couldn't be sent. The AI may already be reading this answer.

summary.title: Looking back
summary.text: {answered, plural, one {One answer} other {# answers}} from this conversation, {personal, plural, =0 {none} one {one} other {#}} of them outside paid work. Here is what came up more than once – nothing you did not confirm yourself.
summary.provisional: {count, plural, one {One answer is not sorted yet} other {# answers are not sorted yet}} – so this is still provisional.
summary.recurringTitle: What came up more than once
summary.recurringText: You confirmed these areas in different stories. That's the most reliable information this method provides – not because it's better, but because it keeps coming up.
summary.inStories: {count, plural, one {in one story} other {in # stories}}
summary.observedTitle: What others come to you for
summary.observedText: From the question about what others repeatedly ask you for help with. That isn't a self-assessment but something others notice in you – and often what you miss in yourself.
summary.wantingTitle: What you want and what you don't
summary.wantingText: Being able to do something isn't the same as wanting to. For a team, that difference matters as much as the ability itself – and it's almost never asked about.
summary.growInto: You would like to take on
summary.singleText: Confirmed in one story. That means it came up once – it's not worth less.
summary.skipped: {count, plural, one {You skipped one question} other {You skipped # questions}}. That counts as an answer, and it stays that way.
summary.withoutArea: {count, plural, one {For one answer} other {For # answers}} no area was found. That says nothing about your story – only that it didn't match our list of terms. You can add areas yourself in your profile.

owned_last.title: Tell me about the last thing you were truly responsible for – through to a clear result, or a deliberate decision to stop.
owned_last.hint: One concrete thing with a beginning and an end. It doesn't have to be big, and deliberately stopping something counts just as much as finishing it.

followUps.whatWasYours: Which part of it was yours specifically – and which part was other people's?
followUps.howYouDecidedDone: How did you decide it was finished, good enough, or no longer worth it?

went_wrong.title: Tell me about something that recently turned out quite differently from what you had planned or hoped.
went_wrong.hint: This is not about blame but about what came after. What you changed afterwards says more about your ability than a success story.

followUps.yourOwnPart: Looking back, what was your own part in it?
followUps.whatChanged: What specifically did you change afterwards?

outside_work.title: Outside of traditional paid work, what have you built, organized or made possible where your own contribution really mattered?
outside_work.hint: A club, your neighborhood, family, friends, volunteering, a move, caring for someone, a festival, a protest. It counts just as much here as a project at work – and it won't show up in any job reference.

followUps.whatYouDidYourself: What exactly did you do yourself?
followUps.howYouNoticedImpact: How did you notice that your contribution made a difference?

in_front_of_group.title: Tell me about a time you had to explain something to people who didn't know you or your topic well – or win them over to it.
in_front_of_group.hint: That could be a stage, a pitch, a conversation with a government office, a first customer, a parent-teacher meeting, or one person you had to convince. Even if it went badly.

followUps.whatYouNeededToUnderstand: What did you have to understand about these people for it to work?
followUps.didYouAdapt: Did you change how you explained or persuaded along the way – and why?

uncomfortable_topic.title: When did you last raise an important, uncomfortable matter even though you expected resistance or tension?
uncomfortable_topic.hint: An unpaid invoice, an expectation, a behavior, a decision nobody wanted to make. At work or in your personal life.

followUps.whyItMattered: Why was it important to you to raise it anyway?
followUps.howYouWentAboutIt: How exactly did you go about it – and what happened afterwards?

people_come_to_you.title: What do others keep asking you for help, advice or support with, even if it isn't officially your job?
people_come_to_you.hint: The outside view. If several people ask you about the same thing, that's a signal that's easy to miss in yourself.

followUps.lastExample: What was the last concrete example?
followUps.whatYouActuallyDo: What specifically do you do there that others find helpful?

would_hand_over.title: What task or responsibility are you carrying right now that you'd rather hand over in the long run?
would_hand_over.hint: Something that gets done because otherwise nobody would do it. This isn't about ability but about what you want – and for a team, that matters just as much.

followUps.whyStillYou: Why are you still doing it yourself at the moment?
followUps.whatSomeoneElseNeeds: What would somebody else have to be able to do or deliver for you to hand it over with a clear conscience?

want_to_own.title: Which responsibility would you like to take on next year, even though today you're not sure you could handle it well on your own?
want_to_own.hint: Something you want to grow into. Saying that openly is worth more in a team than quietly assuming you can handle it.

followUps.whatYouWouldNeed: What would you still need to learn, or experience in practice at least once?

team.title: Skills & responsibility
team.text: Who owns what, where several people want the same thing, and where nobody wants it. This describes the current situation based on your own entries – no rating, no points, no ranking.
team.basis: {contributing} of {members} team members have made entries, {withDepth} of them with an experience level and a responsibility preference. Only those two allow any statement about a role – anyone who has shared less appears here without depth.
team.mapText: One bar per field, one segment per area with entries. Colors show the state, and the same information appears as a number next to it.
team.familyUnspoken: Nobody has said anything about this. That does not mean it is missing.
team.emptyText: This shows the experience level and responsibility preference of members who share with this team. That needs entries on skills – and sharing turned on for this specific team. Each person decides both for themselves; “private” stays private as long as you don't share.

contested.label: Several want to own it
contested.text: Two or more people claim the same responsibility. Who decides here isn't settled yet – that's worth a conversation, not who's better at it.

gap.label: Nobody wants it, nobody can do it
gap.text: Nobody wants responsibility for this and nobody has stated deep experience. This is the only situation that forces a decision: hire, contract it out – or deliberately leave it open and record that.

openPosition.label: Somebody can, nobody wants to
openPosition.text: The skills are there, but nobody wants the responsibility. That's an arrangement to make, not a shortcoming – often it's enough to agree on it for a limited time.

claimedShallow.label: Wanted, not much experience yet
claimedShallow.text: Somebody wants to own this and, by their own account, has not applied it repeatedly yet. That is fine – what matters is that it is said out loud in the team and not treated as settled.

handoverPath.label: Handover possible
handoverPath.text: One person wants to grow into it; another has deep experience and doesn't want to keep the responsibility. That's a transition you can plan.

settled.label: Owned
settled.text: Exactly one person wants it and, by their own account, has depth in it. The others do not want it.

noBasis.label: Too few entries
noBasis.text: Fewer than two people have made a choice here – or they chose “Still unclear”. Turning that into a statement about roles would be guesswork, so there isn't one.

team.teamBasis: {contributing} of {members} team members have made entries, {withDepth} of them with an experience level and a responsibility preference. Depth is visible when someone shares with this team – sharing in another team doesn't count here.

strengths.title: How you work
strengths.text: Sentences about how you work — based on situations you described. For each one, you can say two things: how often it shows up, and what people who've worked with you would say.
strengths.proposalsText: Each with the passage it's based on. None of it counts until you accept it — and you can rewrite it.
strengths.empty: Nothing saved yet. Describe a situation in the interview, or write something yourself.
strengths.addPlaceholder: For example: keeps at it when an agreement does not hold
strengths.addHint: A sentence about the WAY you work, not about you as a person. Not “I'm persistent”, but what you did in a situation.
strengths.selfLabel: How often does this show up for you?
strengths.whoLabel: Who did you have in mind?

gap.others_see_more: Here you think others notice it more than you do. That isn't a mistake — it may be where you could give yourself credit for something others have long seen.
gap.others_see_less: Here you notice it more than you think others do. That isn't a mistake either — maybe you show it where nobody notices.

sourcing.internal_onlyHint: Handing this over means handing over the company.
sourcing.componentHint: Available as a ready-made service — often better than doing it yourself on the side.
sourcing.dependsHint: Whether this belongs in the team depends on what you build.

aboutYou.intro: This is where your founder profile comes together, step by step. You don't have to do it all at once — just add whatever fits right now.

basis.title: You & your background
basis.text: Name, short introduction, region, areas of expertise — what others read about you first. Enter it once and it applies everywhere.

arbeitsweise.title: How you work
arbeitsweise.text: The founder questionnaire: how you make decisions, try things out, disagree and handle open questions. Self-reported, not a test result.

mitbringen.title: What you bring
mitbringen.text: From situations you describe to your skills and experience, through to what you want to own — and what you'd rather leave to someone else.

antrieb.title: What drives you
antrieb.text: Six questions about the themes, problems and changes you keep coming back to. This is the part a CV doesn't show.

ressourcen.title: Network & resources
ressourcen.text: Access, contacts and offers you can bring in. They belong to you, not to a single part of the product.

next.eyebrow: Pick up where you left off

steps.basis: Next, you could add your short introduction.
steps.arbeitsweise: Next, you could fill in the founder questionnaire.
steps.gespraech: Next, you could describe a few situations in the conversation.
steps.faehigkeiten: Next, you could choose the areas you bring something to.
steps.erfahrung: Next, you could record how far you've come in your areas.
steps.verantwortung: Next, you could say what you want to own — and what someone else should.
steps.staerken: Next, you could note which ways of working show up in what you do.
steps.antrieb: Next, you could have the conversation about what drives you.
steps.ressourcen: Next, you could review the access and contacts already identified.

payoff.direction: {count, plural, =1 {One confirmed statement} other {# confirmed statements}} about what drives you.

mark.markedNote: You've marked this area as “done for now”. That doesn't mean finished — you can add to it any time, and the mark stays.
mark.mark: I'm done with this for now

resources.ownText: The network, access and offers you bring. For now, only you can see this.
resources.empty: This is where you can record the network, the access or the resources you bring.
resources.labelHint: One short sentence, {max} characters at most.
resources.fromProposal: Taken from a suggestion — the sentence stays as it stood there.

examples.network: Contacts at clinics in the Berlin area
